title: typesafe, runtime-optimal http routing
blurb: The macro is a plain function named `define` that receives a list of tokens, parses into endpoints, validates for uniqueness, generates a sum type representing each possible route, puts them in a trie, and generates a hand-written dispatcher; there's no runtime routing tree structure like in every other HTTP framework.

blocks.label: route declaration
blocks.code:
$http/routing/define(route) {
  get    home         "/"
  get    events       "/events"
  get    counter      "/counter/events"
  get    big-file     "/static/big-file.json"
  get    starry       "/app/starry-night"
  get    visits       "/visits" ?{ who: ?string }
  post   login        "/login"
  get    game-events  "/game/{id: u64}/events"
  post   game-poke    "/game/{id: u64}/poke"
  delete delete-game  "/game/{id: u64}"
}

blocks.label: macro definition
usage; handling a request
blocks.code:
if route/parse-request(req.head) is {
    :err e -> error-response(e),
    :ok r -> if r is {
      :home -> home-page(),
      :events -> global-events(deps),
      :counter -> counter-events(),
      :game-events .{ id } -> game-events(deps, id),
      :game-poke .{ id } -> game-poke(deps, id),
      :big-file -> big-file(),
      :starry -> response/html("todo"),
      :visits p -> visits(deps, req, p.who),
      :login -> login(req),
      :delete-game p -> response/html("todo ${p.id}"),
    }
  }

title: An embedded html+k1 language, implemented with code-token macros and `eval`
blurb: `html/markup` is just a macro in std. Tags, attributes, k1 expressions, `#for`, and `#if` are parsed while compiling and become calls that directly build up the rendered html; skipping an intermediate AST/DOM tree.

title: compile-time sql queries and schema-driven codegen
blurb: 'dbx' is a k1 sqlite library that will read and execute your schema migrations at compile-time, generate a row type for each table, and insert/update queries; and typecheck your own queries

blocks.label: db schema, the actual sql migrations
blocks.code:
let schema: dbx/schema = dbx/load-schema() | .{ column-types = [
  .{ column = "item.is_group",                                 type-id = types/id[bool] },
  .{ column = "item.growth",                                   type-id = types/id[growth-kind] },
  .{ column = "item.growth_per_year_cents",                    type-id = types/id[span[i64]] },
  .{ column = "item.derivation",                               type-id = types/id[derivation-kind] },
  .{ column = "item.derivation_share_ppm",                     type-id = types/id[span[i64]] },
  .{ column = "item.derivation_enrollment_per_student_cents",  type-id = types/id[span[i64]] },
  .{ column = "item.is_sensitive",                             type-id = types/id[bool] },
  .{ column = "category.flow",                                 type-id = types/id[flow] },
  .{ column = "budget_edit.is_undone",                         type-id = types/id[bool] },
  .{ column = "budget_edit_change.is_inverse",                 type-id = types/id[bool] },
  .{ column = "budget_edit_change.kind",                       type-id = types/id[change-kind] },
] }

title: hot reload
blurb: Put your request handler, or your game tick fn, in an `ns(reload)`, and a hot-reloadable library and API is generated. The reloadable code includes the transitive closure of everything it calls, so you only need your entrypoint(s) to be reloadable!
